findings.text: follow-on: the refused outcome is unreachable on every production signalling path, because no caller of _signal_process_group passes run_dir. Each call site pre-writes the attribution record through _write_sender_record(run_dir, ...) and then calls _signal_process_group(pid, start_time) with no run_dir (dispatch.py:6217/6222, 9890/9895, 10020/10021; promotion.py:3790/3795, 5573/5578; recovery.py:3040/3045, 7384), so inside the guard _write_sender_record(run_dir=None, ...) returns None and writes nothing. A guard refusal therefore leaves only the caller's outcome-less attribution line, exactly the state the node's goal exists to remove; the newly added delivered/refused/failed records are produced only when run_dir is supplied, which only the node's own test does. The read-only routing.py write scope could not thread run_dir into these callers, so the wiring is follow-on work owned by the dispatch/promotion/recovery nodes.

follow-on: evidence_inputs names only the recovery.py call sites (recovery.py:3045, 7384 and the _stop_delivered_reviews pre-write at recovery.py:862) as unable to record a refusal outcome through routing.py alone, but the same is true of dispatch.py:6222, dispatch.py:9895, dispatch.py:10021, promotion.py:3795 and promotion.py:5578, which likewise call _signal_process_group without run_dir; the disclosure understates the gap from one module to four, and the write scope of the node does not include dispatch.py or promotion.py.

item_verdicts.call_sites: read: seven production callers of _signal_process_group at head d6320898 (dispatch.py:6222,9895,10021; promotion.py:3795,5578; recovery.py:3045,7384), each pre-writing an attribution record through _write_sender_record and then calling the guard with no run_dir, plus four signal_worker callers (fleet_supervisor.py:730,735; standing_suite.py:150; routing.py:1585).
item_verdicts.diff: read revision d6320898 against base f91fa54; routing.py +66/-17 (outcome/detail on _write_sender_record, delivered/failed appended in signal_worker, refused written by both guards in _signal_process_group), tests/test_every_signal_leaves_a_sender_record.py +55/-17 adding test_a_refused_signal_records_its_refusal and updating the two existing record assertions from one record to two; the commit touches exactly those two files.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks that each sender record carry an outcome, that a case calling _signal_process_group with a mismatched start time assert the record reads refused, a logged negative control, and zero added failures across the two named test files; all four reproduce here (gate at d6320898 10 passed, base at f91fa54 9 passed, negative control 1 failed 4 passed, zero added failures), but the mechanism is inert on every production path because no caller passes run_dir.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a sender record states whether its signal was delivered or refused; routing.py:1461 signal_worker and routing.py:1530 _signal_process_group now append an outcome record when run_dir is supplied, but no production caller supplies run_dir, so on every real signalling path the outcome is still absent and a refusal is still read as an attributed SIGTERM.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, naming the mechanism, the gate, both arms with machine-readable baseline_suite/after_suite (baseline f91fa54, after d6320898, both completed true, failure_count 0), the negative control and its log, and measurement_module/measurement_cwd; it discloses the coupling under evidence_inputs but names only recovery.py call sites and omits dispatch.py and promotion.py.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are routing.py, the gate test, an evidence fragment and a figure dir; the brief states the done-when names no artifact so no fragment or figure is written, and git show --stat d6320898 lists exactly routing.py and the gate test and nothing else.

justifications.durability: the logged negative control reproduces here (omitting the outcome on the refused record leaves 0 refused records, and test_a_refused_signal_records_its_refusal reddens 1 failed 4 passed EXIT=1), so the added assertion is falsifiable; but no test drives a production call site, so the current state — every _signal_process_group caller omitting run_dir, leaving the refusal record unwritten in production — passes the suite green.
justifications.evidence: the done_when's artefacts reproduce against d6320898: I ran the named gate in the reviewed worktree (10 passed), the base arm log names f91fa54 with 9 passed, the head log names d6320898 with 10 passed, and I reproduced the negative control in a scratch tree (1 failed 4 passed), giving zero added failures (added_failure_count 0, added_failure_ids []); both arms are machine-readable with completed=true.
justifications.fit: the outcome/detail keyword arguments on _write_sender_record, the appended second JSON line and the duplicated guard writes follow the module's existing append-a-dict idiom, and the added names carry no plan, sprint or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: routing.py:1461 signal_worker records delivered/failed and routing.py:1530 _signal_process_group's two guards record refused with the guard's reason, all gated on run_dir being non-None, but grep at head shows no production caller of _signal_process_group passes run_dir (dispatch.py:6222,9895,10021; promotion.py:3795,5578; recovery.py:3045,7384 all call _signal_process_group(pid, start_time)), so outside the test the outcome is never written and the goal is unmet on every real path.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat d6320898 touches exactly the two declared in-scope paths (reckon/crew/routing.py and tests/test_every_signal_leaves_a_sender_record.py), the out-of-scope call sites that would need run_dir are left untouched rather than edited around the fence, and the brief's instruction to write no evidence prose or figure is followed.
